name: Charles Schwab

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Brokerage, wealth and banking firm: clients hold $13.33T in assets across 48.6M accounts; Schwab earns on lending client cash and margin, and on fees.

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: Q3 net revenue $7,171M: net interest 48%, asset management and admin fees 27%, trading 16%, bank deposit account fees 5%, other 4%. Offsetting streams.

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: Millions of retail and RIA clients, no concentration; 40.3M active brokerage accounts supply the cash that funds the bank.

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: Almost entirely US; only $10.9B of non-sovereign foreign holdings, so little currency exposure (revenue split by geography not broken out in the 10-Q).

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Spread on client cash plus margin and bank loans, plus fees; 52% of revenue is not net interest. Rate-sensitive half: NIM 3.04% vs 2.88% a year ago.

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Pre-tax margin 52.7% (49.2% a year ago); adjusted expenses +9% against revenue +17%, so operating leverage is positive. Guidance hit rate not tested.

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Critical input is client cash (tags: fed_funds, 2y, real_spending). Bank deposits fell to $244.1B from $255.7B at year-end as cash sorts into other products; wholesale funding filled the gap: other short-term borrowings $14.2B (was $6.9B), brokerage payables $46.5B (was $25.7B), brokered CDs $3.8B (was $2.0B), FHLB only $2.0B. Supplemental funding is not being paid down, it changed form to fund $187.9B margin loans. Cost pass-through: strong, deposits cost 0.23% against 3.90% asset yield.

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: Scale and low cost, one platform for trading, advice and banking; new: Pledged Asset Lines $37.3B (+59%), Forge private-markets deal closed 2026-03-02 for $636M, crypto and AI assistant launches.

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: Household name for 48.6M accounts; new brokerage accounts 1.2M in Q3 (+9%). Marketing spend per revenue dollar not extracted.

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Core net new assets $190.4B in Q3, +38%, annualised organic growth 5.8%: taking share. Rival data (Fidelity, Vanguard, IBKR, Robinhood) not pulled.

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: $13.33T client assets against over $90T of US investable wealth (company estimate); bank loans $72.3B, +35% yoy; Wealth Advisory flows +55%.

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: ROTCE 44% (Q3) vs 10% cost of equity; buybacks restarted: $3.9B (40.2M shares, about $97 each) in 9 months, dividend +19% to $0.32; consolidated CET1 24.5%, adjusted Tier 1 leverage 7.0% (target 6.75-7.00%). Insider ownership table in DEF 14A not extracted.

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: Not losing relevance (assets +15% yoy). Risks: cash sorting, trading and margin volumes are at cycle highs (daily trades +44%), and margin loans include $60.7B long/short strategy balances funded wholesale.

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: No 8-K Item 4.01/4.02, no NT filings in 3 years, no material weakness found in the 10-Q; SEC comment letters Dec 2023-Jan 2024 (old); non-GAAP add-back only $151M pre-tax; generic regulatory-inquiry language in legal note.

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Overheat: good (trading, margin, higher short rates lift floating yields). Slowdown: fees fall with markets but falling long yields shrink AOCI loss ($11.2B). Hike-driven cash sorting is the weak spot.

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: Category III bank holding company, AOCI excluded from regulatory capital; no pending deal docket found (Forge closed). Easing capital rules a mild tailwind.

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: Reverse residual income: tangible common equity about $27.5B (equity $51.4B less preferred $6.2B, goodwill $12.0B, intangibles $5.7B); price $93.45 gives $161.3B cap, P/TBV 5.9x. At 10% cost of equity and 3% growth that implies ROTCE of about 44%, which equals Q3's peak 44% (9-month 42%, FY25 38%). Excluding AOCI loss, TBV $38.7B, P/TBV 4.2x implies 32% vs actual about 27%. P/E 16.0 trailing (5.85 EPS), forward about 12.0, vs 5-year year-end P/E of 21-26x (2022 22.5, 2023 26.0, 2024 24.1, 2025 21.2); peers JPM 13.3, MS 13.3, IBKR 28.5. Cheap vs own history, no cushion on tangible book.

status_reason: Quality is high, but the price needs a 44% return on tangible equity, the Q3 peak, so there is no cushion on book value despite a low P/E.
the_mistake: Shares are 18% below the 52-week high while net income rose 23% and 9-month EPS 36%: the market trades Schwab as a cash-sorting spread lender, yet net interest is only 48% of revenue and fees, trading and deposit fees are growing faster. Partly offset: record trading and margin volumes are cyclical.
what_makes_market_notice: Q4 results around 2027-01-20 (date from past pattern, not confirmed): core net new assets, sweep cash and NIM; Fed Dec 8-9 decision.

findings.client_cash: Transactional sweep cash $492.8B at September, +$7.1B vs June, after net outflow from bank sweep; bank deposits $244.1B vs $255.7B at Dec 2025
findings.nim: 3.04% Q3 vs 2.88% a year ago; 2.97% 9-month vs 2.69%
findings.supplemental_funding: FHLB $2.0B (small); not paid down, replaced by short-term borrowings $14.2B and brokerage payables to fund margin
findings.aoci: Loss $11.2B vs $11.0B at Dec 2025, largely unrealized MBS loss ($3.9B on $38.9B agency MBS AFS) plus HTM transfer losses; excluded from regulatory capital
findings.buybacks: Restarted: $500M in Q3, $3.9B in 9 months under $20B authorisation
findings.td_integration: Nothing in the Q3 10-Q on remaining TD Ameritrade synergies; TD Bank fully exited its stake in 2025; Forge integration under way (costs $49M 9-month)

feedback.note: Sweep cash grew in Q3 and bank deposit account fee revenue rose 40% on higher net yields, consistent with the Overheat read; cash sorting out of bank deposits (-$11.6B YTD) is the risk if the Fed hikes. Trading volume +44% and VIX spike support the volatility read.
